column1: # PB-APP-9 traceability: every error class the facade exports -> the state the user is
# shown and what they can do about it. Enforced in THREE directions, none of which trusts
# this file:
#   - mobile/s16_taxonomy_test.go   class_const and token are set-compared against
#                                   mobile/testdata/exported_surface.golden, and each token
#                                   is read from the CONSTANT's source rather than from
#                                   here -- so a drifted row fails instead of misrouting;
#   - android/gate/s16_ui_test.go   rendered_state is set-compared against the Kotlin
#                                   `enum class ErrorState`, and every token must appear
#                                   verbatim in the Kotlin sources;
#   - mobile/conformance/s16_errorstates_test.go  every row is reachable: an adversarial
#                                   state matrix sweeps the whole golden surface and no
#                                   error may land outside this table.
# Columns: class_const <TAB> token <TAB> sentinel <TAB> rendered_state <TAB> remedy <TAB> requirement <TAB> note
# `sentinel` is the Go error IDENTITY the class classifies, or "-" for a class the facade
# authors itself. A class that classifies MORE than one identity lists them comma-separated;
# the column is not exhaustive (ErrClassNoLease also absorbs ErrLeaseExpired and ErrGapPending)
# and names the identities PB-APP-10 requires to be told apart.
# `rendered_state` is a constant of dev.swarm.phone.ui.ErrorState.
# `remedy` is what the user (or the machine) must do; the two of PB-APP-10 are
# re_pair / machine_regrant and they may never collapse. There were THREE until ADR-007 B133:
# `authenticate` left with its subject, because all phone-side user authentication is removed
# and a remedy naming an act the product can no longer offer is advice nobody can carry out.
# Its row -- ErrClassReauthRequired / REAUTH_REQUIRED, whose sentinel was
# crypto.ErrKeyAuthRequired -- went in the same change as mobile/relay.go's connReauthRequired,
# the Kotlin ConnectionState and ErrorState entries, and Remedy.AUTHENTICATE.
# crypto stays FROZEN and still raises crypto.ErrKeyAuthRequired, so the identity did not go
# with the row: it is now classified by ErrClassRepairRequired, in all three places that route
# it -- mobile/relay.go's dial switch (connRepairRequired), mobile/errorclass.go's
# stampErrorClass, and dev.swarm.phone.PhoneRuntime.routeCustodyVerdict, which puts
# KeyCustodyException.UserAuthenticationRequired in the same arm as KeyPermanentlyInvalidated.
# The class ErrClassReauthRequired is deleted, not merely unmapped: an exported class this
# table has no row for reaches the screen as an opaque exception, and the Kotlin router answers
# UNKNOWN for its token -- fail-safe, and still the failure PB-APP-9 exists to stop.
#class_const
column7: note

column1: ErrClassUnknown
column7: RESERVED. App.ErrorClass answers this for a message the facade did not produce, and for nothing else. It is what makes the exhaustiveness sweep a real assertion: a classifier that could not say "I do not know this" would satisfy every other check by answering one class for everything.

column1: ErrClassInternal
column7: A panic caught at the JNI boundary, or a foreign error identity nothing routes. Never the user's fault and never has a user action, which is why it must not share a state with anything that does.

column1: ErrClassInvalidRequest
column7: A screen passed something the facade cannot use: an empty session id, a nil spec, a stream name that is not one of the four repair channels. Same remedy as INTERNAL and a different state, because the app is otherwise healthy and one call was wrong.

column1: ErrClassNotFound
column7: A lookup that legitimately misses -- a session no longer in the roster, a snapshot never received, an index past the end of a handle. Distinct from INVALID_REQUEST: nothing is wrong with the call, the thing is simply gone.

column1: ErrClassClosed
column7: A call on an App the Android lifecycle already closed. Its own class because it is the one failure a screen fixes by doing nothing: the next launch constructs a new App.

column1: ErrClassOffline
column7: The transport: not started, no connection yet, or the relay refused or dropped the call. The ONE class for which a spinner is honest -- every other waiting state here has something the user must do.

column1: ErrClassNotPaired
column7: The phone holds no machine destination. NOT the same as REPAIR_REQUIRED: nothing is broken and no owner has revoked anything -- this handset has simply never completed a pairing that pinned a destination.

column1: ErrClassStateCorrupt
column7: PB-STATE-4's fail-closed refusal of a durable blob that will not load. It was ErrClassInternal until S18b, i.e. remedy report_bug over a state the owner CAN recover from -- the brick expressed as a screen. Its remedy is its own because it is TWO acts and neither alone works: the user clears the app's data, and the OWNER unregisters the device at the machine, or the re-pair the advice ends in is refused (PB-KEY-3). It does not offer the pairing flow: there is no App to offer it from, the blob having failed Resume.

column1: ErrClassDeviceUnsupported
column7: PB-KEY-8's two refusals -- a capability the handset does not provide, and a key read back WEAKER than requested. Raised on the Android side (KeyCustodyException.PlatformCapabilityMissing / KeystoreDowngrade, routed by PhoneRuntime), so the sentinel column is "-": the Go facade has no identity for a Keystore read-back. Same remedy as INTERNAL and a different state, for INVALID_REQUEST's reason inverted: the APP is healthy and the platform is not, so a message blaming the app is false. It must never be re_pair -- a re-pair re-provisions the same key on the same handset and returns to this screen, which is PB-APP-10's forbidden loop reached through the remedy.

column1: ErrClassUnreconciled
column7: PB-SYNC-7's fail-closed refusal of mutating ops until the machine publishes its rollback authorities. Reads keep working throughout, so the screen shows a banner and not an error page.

column1: ErrClassAwaitingKey
column7: No epoch content key, and the grant has NOT been proved lost. This is the ordinary first-launch window; rendering it as GRANT_LOST would send a healthy user to the machine for a key that is already on its way.

column1: ErrClassGrantLost
column7: The one remedy the USER cannot perform. It may never collapse into REPAIR_REQUIRED: BeginPairing fail-fasts while this device is registered (PB-STATE-10), so "pair again" is advice that cannot be carried out and the only exit left is physical access to the machine.

column1: ErrClassRepairRequired
column7: PERMANENT. The Keystore key cannot be used and nothing done on the device brings it back. The token is the one Kotlin has matched on since S14 (GoCustodyFailure.KEY_INVALIDATED_TOKEN) and is deliberately not re-spelled; a drifted copy falls through to UNKNOWN, which tells a user whose key is gone to try again forever. TWO SENTINELS SHARE IT after ADR-007 B133: crypto.ErrKeyInvalidated is the destroyed key, and crypto.ErrKeyAuthRequired is a key gated on an authentication this product no longer performs -- raised only by an install provisioned before B133, whose AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG content KEK KeystoreCustodyBootstrap.ensure does not re-request on upgrade. For that handset a re-pair discards the alias and re-provisions without an authenticator, so re_pair is the true remedy and not a bucket. It does NOT extend to phonecore.ErrGrantLost: that one the user cannot perform at all.

column1: ErrClassRevoked
column7: The OWNER removed this device. It shares REPAIR_REQUIRED's remedy and not its cause, which is why it is a class of its own: the machine still holds a registration the owner must clear before a re-pair can succeed. Without this row a revoked phone redials every 250 ms behind a spinner forever.

column1: ErrClassNoLease
column7: The machine has not confirmed a control lease, so every keystroke is refused. The screen's remedy is to offer take-control; a retry is the one thing that cannot help. Since Wave R6, PB-APP-3's Stop no longer rides this class: it is the signed turn_interrupt op and needs no lease.

column1: ErrClassStaleTurn
column7: Wave R6: the daemon refused a composer send because expected_turn no longer names the session's current turn -- the conversation moved on between render and tap. An ORDINARY race, never a bug report: the composer keeps the draft, shows the gentle notice, and the user re-reads the fresh transcript and sends again. The wire code (Outcome.Code stale_turn) and this class name the same state; the Kotlin composer renders it via ComposerModel.noticeFor("STALE_TURN").

column1: ErrClassRateLimited
column7: A bound this phone enforces on itself (the section 6.0 resync budget) or the relay enforces on it. Retryable only after waiting: "asking harder" is exactly what the bound exists to stop.

column1: ErrClassPairingFailed
column7: The class for errors the pairing VERBS return. The pairing attempt's own terminal state is on the Pairing handle and is finer grained (PB-PAIR-5's five values); this is what a screen shows when the call itself failed.

column1: ErrClassPairingCodeInvalid
column7: The ten typed characters are not a short code. It is SPLIT OFF PAIRING_FAILED and not folded into it (agents-tracker-ksvb.5): that row's sentence sends the user back to their machine to start again, and nothing here has started -- the code is still on the machine's screen and the act is to read it once more. The remedy is retry_pairing rather than pair: the user is already in the flow, and offering to open it again is the step they are standing on.

column1: ErrClassRelayUnknown
column7: A typed code with no relay to complete it: this handset has never scanned a QR and none was pasted beside the code. It is the phone MISSING a fact rather than any call failing, which is why it may not share PAIRING_FAILED's row -- there is nothing to retry. The two acts that supply the fact are the scan and the paste, and the copy names both because a handset with no camera can only do the second.

column1: ErrClassRelayAddressInvalid
column7: A relay address in the wrong SHAPE, refused by mobile/pairing.go's relayAddress before anything is dialled. It is its own row and not RELAY_UNKNOWN's for exactly the fact the user holds: one person has no address at all and the other has typed one wrong, so telling the second to scan a QR ignores what is on their own screen. Caught here it is a sentence naming the shape; passed through it is a confirm step asking the user to approve their own typo.
